mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in FEDFUNDS above 5% over three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE above 4% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in INDPRO below 98 for three consecutive months indicates weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in UNRATE above 6% and a fall in PAYEMS below 137,000,000 in the same month signals labor market overheating with employment stagnation, which increases cost pressures without output growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 6% AND PAYEMS < 137000000 in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.4%) in at least 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in HOUST above 950,000 units for two consecutive months indicates a surge in new single-family home sales, reflecting stronger household demand and a positive outlook for consumer spending, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening in monetary policy and inflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 12mo MA AND CPIAUCSL > 12mo MA in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 55% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in RSAFS above 450,000,000 over six consecutive months signals robust retail sales growth, reflecting strong consumer demand and supporting corporate earnings, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered periods.
